subject: Veridian Labs MAP: cost acceptance, batching & caching sanity checks
messages:
From: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@veridianlabs.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-11T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: MAP & cost model details for pilot evaluation

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — Veridian is excited about the latency numbers, but procurement and engineering asked for a short Mutual Action Plan that explicitly calls out the unit economics assumptions we'll validate during the pilot. Specifically: tokens/$ assumptions, expected caching behavior for our prompt templates, and the batching profile at 99th vs p50 latencies. Can you share a MAP draft and the evaluation plan you'd like us to run against the pilot traffic?

We'd like to close the commercial terms within two weeks after the pilot validation — procurement will want a clear acceptance checklist. Attaching our initial usage profile in a follow-up email.

Alex
Principal AI Engineer
Veridian Labs

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@veridianlabs.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-11T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & cost model details for pilot evaluation

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. I put together a short MAP draft and an evaluation checklist (attached: veridian_map_draft_v1.pdf) plus a token econ spreadsheet (token_econ_spreadsheet.xlsx) with the assumptions we used for similar early-stage pilots. Key points up front:

- Proposed pilot duration: 14 days (1 week warm-up + 1 week steady-state)
- Acceptance criteria: throughput targets met, 95th token latency < target, and unit cost within 25% of our estimate in the spreadsheet.
- Unit-econ assumptions called out in the MAP: tokens per request, cache hit rate (prefix caching), batching factor distribution, and quantized model profile.

Ben and Marissa — can you quickly review the MAP and confirm the batching/caching assumptions below before I send to Veridian? I want to ensure the acceptance criteria map cleanly to the metrics Veridian's team will collect.

Naomi
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@veridianlabs.com>
Date: 2028-03-12T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & cost model details for pilot evaluation

Naomi / Alex — quick notes on the spreadsheet and MAP assumptions (my edits in the attached sheet):

1) Tokens / $ baseline: we used an estimated effective tokens-per-second (TPS) and GPU-hour cost for the quantized 7B model variant. For Veridian's profile (avg prompt 420 tokens, avg response 110 tokens) the blended tokens/request is ~530 tokens. At current Dedicated pricing that's ~0.00065 $/token effective (spreadsheet calc).

2) Caching: our conservative default for prefix (prompt) caching hit rate in pilot MAPs is 22% for templated prompts with variable fields. If Veridian's templates are highly repetitive (same prompt + filled slots) we should assume 45-60% hit rate. Recommend instrumenting prefix keys in the first 48 hours to validate. MAP acceptance gate: observed cache_hit_rate >= 30% over steady-state window (final 7 days).

3) Batching profile / latency tradeoffs: the MAP should record batching factor distribution (p10/p50/p95) and token-latency. We typically see p50 latency within target with on-demand batching (batching factor 4-8) and p95 pushes up depending on queueing; add a hard SLO allowance: p95 token-latency <= 2x p50 during steady-state. For acceptance, require p50 <= 180ms and p95 <= 400ms for the primary route.

4) Fallbacks: include an automatic fallback to a smaller 3B quantized variant for sustained queueing > 1.5x baseline capacity. That keeps availability while preserving cost. Document cost delta in the spreadsheet as a scenario.

I'll send a marked-up spreadsheet (done) and suggest a quick call to align on instrumentation keys.

-ben
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@veridianlabs.com>
Date: 2028-03-13T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & cost model details for pilot evaluation

Couple of commercial notes to align with procurement:

- Pricing guardrails: for pilot we typically discount unit price by 20% but cap monthly spend exposure. For the MAP acceptance, we can offer a trial credit that absorbs the first 2 weeks if unit costs exceed the spreadsheet estimate by >20%.
- Mutual acceptance checklist should list: (a) cache instrumented, (b) traffic profile captured, (c) billing estimate reconciliation signed, (d) post-pilot rollout recommendation.
- Procurement ask: include a short procure path (PO + NDA equivalent) and target legal turnaround of 5 business days after we hand off the finalized SOW.

Sending this back to finalize with Naomi. If Veridian wants a shorter close timeline we can compress to 7 business days but will need procurement alignment early.

-marissa
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@veridianlabs.com>, procurement@veridianlabs.com
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-15T16:28:00-07:00
Subject: Final MAP + evaluation timeline and next steps (attachments)

Alex / procurement team — attaching the MAP draft and token econ workbook. Summary & next steps: 

1) MAP & evaluation plan: 14-day pilot (start window: next week), instrumentation checklist included in the PDF. Acceptance gates: cache_hit_rate >= 30% steady-state, tokens-per-request within +/-25% of estimate, p50/p95 token-latency targets as noted by Ben.

2) Instrumentation: please share a small sample of production-like traffic (anonymized) and confirm the template set we should instrument for prefix keys. Ben will validate keys in the first 48 hours.

3) Commercials: pilot credit covers first 2 weeks up to $12,000. If acceptance criteria met we aim to execute the SOW within 7 business days of sign-off; legal turnaround target is 5 business days post-SOW.

4) Timeline to close: pilot start target: 2028-03-20, pilot end: 2028-04-03, SOW sign by 2028-04-10 (if accepted). If procurement needs faster cadence, tell us and we'll prioritize.

Please confirm receipt and whether procurement is okay with the PO + SOW path. If you're good, I'll upload the MAP to HubSpot and share the DocuSign draft.

Best,
Naomi
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: veridian_map_draft_v1.pdf (MAP + acceptance checklist), token_econ_spreadsheet.xlsx (model with scenario rows for caching / fallback).
